This appeal coming on for admission this day, the Court

 Order

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved of award dated 30/07/2022 passed by the Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in MACC No.1352/2019 whereby learned Claims Tribunal has allowed the claim petition and has awarded compensation in favour of the complainants on account of death of Rajendra Ahirwar, who was travelling in the offending Truck bearing registration No.MP-22-H-0783, as a cleaner in the Truck.

sentences.text: It is submitted that said Truck was carrying 300 goats.

Dimension of the Truck was 22 ft. x 7.25 ft.
measuring 159.5 sq. ft. or roughly 14.82 sq. mts.
It is submitted that firstly there is evidence of the Officer from the RTO.
Shri Tulsi Ram Solanki (P.W.-1) has clearly deposed that separate permit is required for transporting animals in a goods vehicle.
The vehicle requires a separate permit and a separate cabin.
This evidence of Shri Tulsi Ram Solanki, Assistant Grade - III in the Office of RTO, Seoni has remained unrebutted.
Shri Utpal Ghosh (P.W.-2), Deputy Manager of the Insurance Company has also deposed that the vehicle was not insured to carry animals.
RTO is required to issue separate permit and that permit was not available with the offending vehicle.

It is pointed out that Rule 81 of M.P. Motor Vehicles Rules, 1994 provides in sub-Rule (1) that no cattle shall be carried in a goods carriage in a public place unless :- (i) in the case of goats, sheep,
deer or pigs or a minimum floor space of one square meter per five heads of such cattle is provided in the vehicle.

It is also submitted that as per provisions contained in Central Motor Vehicle Rules,
1989 (for short 'the Rules of 1989) has amended upto date w.e.f. 01/01/2016, Rule 125E deals with special requirements of motor vehicles used for transporting of animals.

It is provided that not only New India Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Hema Ahirwar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15949388/
2 separate permit will be required, but also the cabins should contain a space of 0.3 sq. mts. per sheep or goat.
Since, there was violation of permit conditions, therefore, no award could have been passed against the Insurance Company and at best it could make against the owner/driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Thus, placing reliance on the decisions in case of Lakhmi Chand (supra), is submitted that there is no violation of the policy and the appeal deserves to be dismissed and be dismissed.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, accident took place on 27/03/2019 when deceased Rajendra Ahirwar was travelling in Truck No. MP-202-H-0783 from Jatara to Hyderabad, carrying goats.
Accident took place at about 6 am at Shamshabad Road near Bairasiya when Truck turned turtle, deceased suffered injuries and died.
Shri Mishra, learned counsel for respondents No.6 and 7 has not pointed out from the record that there was no permit for carrying goats.

As per the requirements of Rule 125E of the Rules of 1989,
which provides that after 01/01/2016 motor vehicles being used for transporting of animals will have to have special features as per the standards laid down by Bureau o f Indian Standards 15-14904:2007; or 15-5238:2001; or IS 5236:1982.
Sub- rule (2) provides that the body of such motor vehicle shall have permanent partition and the animals will be kept in such permanent partitions.
Sub-clause (iii) of sub-rule (2) of Rule 125E provides that each sheep or goat will have an area of 0.3 sq. mts. to itself.
Sub-rule (4) provides that the RTO in terms of the provisions contained in sub-Rule (2) shall issue special permits for carrying of animals in the goods vehicle.

An exception has been made that if two milking animals are taken along with their calves for local transport, then such provisions of Rule 125E will not be applicable if they are transported in N vehicle or agricultural tractor.
Thus, it is evident that the requirement of rules after 01/01/2016 is to obtain a special permit, modify the vehicle or to fulfill the requirements of Bureau o f Indian Standards.
Same is the requirement of Rule 81 of the M.P. Motor Vehicles Rules, 1994.

sentences.text: 3 In the present case, there is no permit for transport of animals nor there is any modification in the vehicle for the purpose of transportation of goat/sheep.

In view of such facts and the evidence of Shri Solanki, it is evident that there is a fundamental breach of the policy conditions and vehicle was being plied without special permit meant for this purpose.

Thus, taking over all fact situation into consideration, since the insurance company has proved not only breach of permit but also violation of other terms and conditions, Insurance Company could not have been fastened with the liability to satisfy the award without leaving an option with it to recover the same from the owner/driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, in the light of the law laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pappu Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba, (2018) 3 SCC 208, I am of the opinion that impugned award needs to be modified.
